corpus.title: Developing Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) based LLM Systems from PDFs: An Experience Report
corpus.page_note: The estimate counts PDF pages 2-34 as content and excludes the title/abstract page, references (page 35), and appendix (page 36).
corpus.filter_metadata: For filter questions, populate the chunk metadata field section from the printed section or subsection heading. Apply the filter only when the question supplies that section.

questions.question: Why can a traditional generative model give outdated answers?
questions.expected_answer: Its internal knowledge has a fixed cutoff based on its training data.
questions.evidence_quote: Traditional generative models, such as GPT, BERT, or T5 are trained on massive datasets but have a fixed internal knowledge cut off based on their training data.

questions.question: Which two NLP components does RAG combine?
questions.expected_answer: Information Retrieval (IR) and Natural Language Generation (NLG).
questions.evidence_quote: The concept of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) models is built on integrating two core components of NLP: Information Retrieval (IR) and Natural Language Generation (NLG).

questions.question: What do the document embeddings allow the RAG system to do?
questions.expected_answer: Capture text meaning and perform similarity searches.
questions.evidence_quote: These vector embeddings capture the semantic meaning of the text, allowing the system to perform similarity searches.

questions.question: How does the retriever find content for an incoming query?
questions.expected_answer: It embeds the query like the documents and searches the vector store for the most relevant chunks.
questions.evidence_quote: When a Query is input into the system, it is first transformed into a vector embedding, similar to the documents in the vector store. The Retriever component then performs a search within the vector store to identify and retrieve the most relevant chunks of information related to the query.

questions.question: What is combined in the context-infused prompt sent to the language model?
questions.expected_answer: The original user query and the retrieved relevant content.
questions.evidence_quote: The context-infused prompt, consisting of the original user query combined with the retrieved relevant content is provided to a Large Language Model (LLM) like GPT, T5 or Llama.

questions.question: What are two drawbacks of fine-tuning identified in the paper?
questions.expected_answer: It is computationally expensive and can overfit when the dataset is too narrow, reducing generalizability.
questions.evidence_quote: Fine-tuning is computationally expensive and often requires substantial resources for initial training. Additionally, it risks overfitting if the dataset is too narrow, making the model less generalizable.

questions.question: Why do complex PDF layouts challenge RAG systems?
questions.expected_answer: They complicate text extraction, and RAG systems rely on clean, structured text for high-quality retrieval.
questions.evidence_quote: These complexities challenge RAG systems, which rely on clean, structured text for high-quality retrieval.

questions.question: With section=Effective Chunking for Retrieval, what kind of boundaries should semantic chunking follow?
questions.expected_answer: Logical divisions in the text, such as paragraphs or sections, so chunks retain context.
questions.evidence_quote: Instead of splitting text arbitrarily, use semantic chunking based on logical divisions within the text, such as paragraphs or sections. This ensures that each chunk retains its context

questions.question: What should determine chunk size for a document?
questions.expected_answer: The content type and the model's input limitations.
questions.evidence_quote: Adjust the chunk size according to the content type and the model's input limitations.

questions.question: Name examples of irrelevant PDF text that preprocessing should remove.
questions.expected_answer: Headers, footers, page numbers, and repeating text that does not contribute to the document's meaning.
questions.evidence_quote: clean up non-relevant content like headers, footers, page numbers, and any repeating text that doesn't contribute to the document's meaning.

questions.question: Which PDF metadata examples does the paper say can add context to retrieval?
questions.expected_answer: The author, title, and creation date.
questions.evidence_quote: PDFs often contain metadata (such as the author, title, and creation date) and annotations that provide additional context

questions.question: How does the paper recommend handling errors during PDF processing?
questions.expected_answer: Use try-except blocks to manage potential errors and log issues for later analysis.
questions.evidence_quote: Use try-except blocks to manage potential errors during PDF processing. This ensures the application continues running smoothly and logs any issues for later analysis.

questions.question: What should PDF-processing logs capture, and why?
questions.expected_answer: Successes, failures, and anomalies, to help debug and optimize the application.
questions.evidence_quote: Implement logging to capture detailed information about the PDF processing steps, including successes, failures, and any anomalies. This is important for debugging and optimizing the application over time.

questions.question: With section=Common Mistakes and Best Practices, what default chunk size and overlap does the paper report for OpenAI Vector Stores?
questions.expected_answer: A maximum chunk size of 800 tokens and an overlap of 400 tokens.
questions.evidence_quote: By default OpenAI uses a max chunk size tokens of 800 and chunk overlap tokens of 400 to chunk the file(s) for Vector Stores.

questions.question: With section=Common Mistakes and Best Practices, how can adding context to a query improve retrieval?
questions.expected_answer: It can improve retrieval quality; relevance feedback or pseudo-relevance feedback can refine search results.
questions.evidence_quote: Incorporate additional contextual information when forming queries to improve retrieval quality. Using techniques like relevance feedback or pseudo-relevance feedback can help refine search results.

questions.question: Which embedding model is used in the paper's FAISS example, and what kinds of tasks is it described as suitable for?
questions.expected_answer: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2; semantic search and text similarity.
questions.evidence_quote: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 is a compact, fast transformer model that generates sentence embeddings for tasks like semantic search and text similarity.

questions.question: What suggestion did a participant make about sensitive data in OpenAI Vector Store?
questions.expected_answer: Add a warning about sensitive data in OpenAI Vector Store.
questions.evidence_quote: One notable suggestion was to include a warning regarding sensitive data in OpenAI vector store.

questions.question: What technical issue did workshop participants report when using the guide?
questions.expected_answer: Copying code from the PDF caused errors because of line breaks.
questions.evidence_quote: The most common issues raised were technical, most of them related to copying from PDF file generating errors as number of lines.

questions.question: What does integrating a knowledge graph aim to improve in RAG systems?
questions.expected_answer: Factual accuracy and reasoning capabilities.
questions.evidence_quote: This integration aims to improve the factual accuracy and reasoning capabilities of the models

questions.question: With section=Discussion, what two kinds of capabilities are proposed to make future RAG models more versatile?
questions.expected_answer: Cross-lingual retrieval and multimodal data processing.
questions.evidence_quote: Incorporating cross-lingual retrieval and multimodal data processing can make RAG models more versatile and applicable to a wider range of global and multimedia tasks.
